history.summary: One of Tinsukia's most prominent temples, dedicated to Lord Shiva (Shivalinga) as the main shrine, with subsidiary shrines for Hanuman and Radha-Krishna within the complex. According to a documentary video, it was established in 1965 and built over two years by Late Ganoatrai, Gopiram and Shri Murarilal Rashiwasia of Tinsukia. The complex sits on Makum Road (AT Road / NH 37) at Bhimpara, Hukanpukhuri Gaon, about 1 km from the Tinsukia bus stand; it is known for its large white meditative Shiva statue, landscaped gardens, musical fountains, divine wall paintings of Hindu stories, and a central pond with fish and turtles. No conflict with the CSV town or state.

name: Shiv Dham
town_description: Tinsukia is a major industrial and commercial city in Upper Assam, often called the gateway to the Dibru-Saikhowa National Park and the surrounding tea country. It grew around the oil, tea, timber and coal trades of the region and is known for several notable Hindu temples, including the bell temple Tilinga Mandir nearby.

travel.airport: Dibrugarh Airport (Mohanbari), about 41-45 km away (daily flights from Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Bengaluru)
travel.railway: Tinsukia (New Tinsukia Junction, Hijuguri) railway station - the nearest major railhead
travel.road: On Makum Road / Assam Trunk Road (NH 37), Bhimpara; about 1 km from the Tinsukia bus stand

visitor_information.best_time: November to February (pleasant winter weather); Maha Shivaratri for the grand celebrations
